blocking_findings.label: blocker
blocking_findings.what: Bundle-generation stamping uses an uncoordinated read → temp-write → rename sequence while heartbeat renewal independently uses the same sequence.
blocking_findings.why: Concurrent fire-and-forget heartbeat beats can read an old lock before a successful roll stamps its generation, then rename their stale snapshot afterward. That loses the new generation, causing repeat rolls; it violates AC5's no-lost-updates requirement. Readback at lines 202-218 only observes the immediate write and cannot prevent a later stale heartbeat rename.
blocking_findings.fix: Serialize owner-local lock mutations (heartbeat renewal and generation stamp) through one per-lock critical section, preserve the latest lock fields on each write, and add an interleaving test proving a stale heartbeat cannot overwrite a completed generation stamp.

wisdom_candidates.content: Temp-file-plus-rename makes an individual lock write atomic, but it does not provide compare-and-swap semantics. Concurrent read-modify-write paths need an explicit shared serialization or ownership/version guard to prevent lost fields.

documents.proposal:
## Proposal: Bundle-hash staleness as a first-class worker.lock reclaim trigger

### Approach

1. **Stamp a build hash into the worker bundle.** Emit a stable content/build hash (e.g. from `build:worker`) discoverable at runtime by the worker process and by the plugin host at session start.
2. **Record the running worker's bundle hash in `worker.lock`** (extend `WorkerLockContentsV2` with `bundle_hash`), written on acquire and preserved across heartbeats.
3. **Add a stale-bundle reclaim path.** On session start / worker election, if the deployed-bundle hash != the lock's recorded `bundle_hash`, treat the lock as stale: signal the current worker to exit gracefully and re-elect with the new bundle (same path proven by `rq-temporalConcurrentLoad01.2` worker-kill → respawn-elect).

### Why this shape

- Reuses existing `worker-lock.ts` / `worker-heartbeat.ts` / respawn-elect machinery rather than a new mechanism.
- Makes "stale bundle" structural (hash comparison) instead of an invisible time-based hazard — aligns with structural-correctness (P33).
- Graceful roll preserves in-flight serialization guarantees; no forced multi-session disruption.

### Scope guards

- OOP worker model only (Bun hosts). In-process (Node hosts) already avoids the hazard.
- Must not break the live-holder singleton guarantee for the same-bundle case (no thrash).
- Cross-session: a redeploy should roll peer-session workers on their next election tick, not force-kill live peers mid-workflow.

### Acceptance signal

After redeploy, a running OOP worker on the old bundle is detected via hash mismatch and re-elected onto the new bundle automatically, with no lost updates and no manual `adv_temporal_worker_restart`.
documents.problemStatement:
## Problem

On Bun plugin hosts (opencode's shipping runtime), the ADV Temporal worker runs out-of-process as a Node child loading `dist/temporal/worker.js`. When the bundle is rebuilt/redeployed (`pnpm run build:worker` + `deploy-local.sh`), already-running worker children keep the OLD bundle in memory — Node loads the bundle once at process start and never reloads it.

The `worker.lock` singleton is held by the alive parent session pid, so singleton re-election sees a live holder and does NOT spawn a fresh worker with the new bundle. Heartbeat-staleness reclaim (`tryReclaimStaleLock` / `isHeartbeatStale`, 60s grace) only fires when the holder DIES or goes unserviceable — never for an alive-but-stale-bundle worker.

## Evidence (2026-07-15)

- Deployed `dist/temporal/worker.js` mtime 17:18:40.
- Three live worker.js processes (pids 2235009, 2259292, 2266205) started at ~17:06/17:15/17:17 — all before the redeploy — executing stale workflow/activity code.
- Multi-session multiplies the hazard: N sessions = N independently-stale workers, each silently on old code until manual restart.

## Impact

Redeploy silently leaves every already-running session on old code. Behavior diverges across sessions; bug fixes and workflow determinism changes don't take effect until each session is manually restarted. This is a correctness/consistency hazard, acknowledged in-code at `in-process-worker.ts:22` ("no stale-bundle hazards" cited as the in-process advantage).

## Desired outcome

Redeploy should gracefully auto-roll running out-of-process workers to the new bundle without manual per-session restarts, reusing the existing lock/heartbeat/respawn-elect machinery.
documents.agreement:
## Agreement — autoRollStaleWorkerBundle

### Objectives
1. A redeploy/rebuild of `dist/temporal/worker.js` causes running out-of-process (OOP) workers to roll onto the new bundle automatically — no manual `adv_temporal_worker_restart` or session restart.
2. The same-bundle case must not thrash: a live holder on the current bundle keeps the singleton, no reclaim churn.
3. Peer sessions roll on their next election tick; no force-kill of a live peer worker mid-workflow.

### Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1** `worker.lock` V2 (`WorkerLockContentsV2`) carries a `bundle_hash`, written on acquire and preserved across heartbeats.
- **AC2** A stable content hash of the deployed worker bundle is computable at runtime (hash of `dist/temporal/worker.js`, or a build-emitted stamp).
- **AC3** On session start/election (`plugin-init.ts`), deployed-bundle hash ≠ lock `bundle_hash` ⇒ lock treated as stale ⇒ graceful reclaim + re-elect on the new bundle.
- **AC4** Deployed hash == lock `bundle_hash` ⇒ live holder retained, no reclaim (singleton preserved, no thrash).
- **AC5** Reclaim reuses the existing respawn-elect path; no lost updates under concurrent load (`rq-temporalConcurrentLoad01` preserved).
- **AC6** In-process worker path (Node hosts) is unaffected.
- **AC7** Unit tests cover hash-mismatch reclaim + same-hash no-op; existing `worker-lock` / `worker-heartbeat` tests stay green.

### Constraints
- OOP model only (Bun hosts). Replay determinism preserved. `workflows.ts` worker-bundle import-graph rules respected (no new `node:*`/tools reach; no `defineUpdate`).

### Avoidances
- No time-only staleness as the sole trigger. No forced kill of live peer workers mid-workflow. No change to the fixed `worker.js` output path the spawner expects unless the spawner is updated in lockstep.

### Out of scope
- SQLite→Postgres persistence backend. In-process worker migration. The `/tmp` test-server leak (change `reapLeakedTestServers`).
documents.design:
## Design — autoRollStaleWorkerBundle (revised after design-validator caution)

### Architecture context (verified)
- OOP worker = single Node child (`worker-multi.ts` `spawnChild`) polling the project queue, script `dist/temporal/worker.js`, which loads sibling `dist/temporal/workflows.js`.
- Singleton election (`plugin-init.ts::resolveWorkerSingletonPlan` L89-106, spawn L209-285) runs **only at session init**. Alive fresh-heartbeat owner retains ownership; reclaim (`worker-lock.ts` L104-126) only takes over dead-pid or stale-V2-heartbeat.
- Heartbeat (`worker-heartbeat.ts`) owner-local, 10s, `beatNow()` fire-and-forget (L85-87).
- Deploy = `rsync -a --delete` (no `--inplace`) → single-file writes land via temp+rename (atomic per file), but the **multi-file bundle set is not atomic**.

### Root mechanism (validator-confirmed): owner-driven self-roll
Preferred over new-session reclaim (which would weaken alive-owner lock semantics / add split-brain). Owner is the only live actor; it rolls its own child. Confirmed sound: a fresh Node child = fresh disk module load; Temporal Workflow state is durable server-side so kill+respawn on the same task queue loses no Workflow progress (in-flight Activities may retry — Activities must tolerate retry, which is an existing obligation).

### Validator blockers folded into design
1. **First-class `restartChild` lifecycle (blocker 1).** Do NOT reuse parent `shutdown()` (sets `shuttingDown=true`, suppresses respawn) or the crash-respawn path (monotonic `restartCount`, exhausts after 3 → intentional rolls would consume crash budget). Add a dedicated intentional-restart op in `worker-multi.ts`: graceful child stop → relaunch → readiness, leaving the crash counter unchanged.
2. **Explicit `shutdownGraceTime` (blocker 2).** SDK default is **0**, not 5s (the 5s `MULTI_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS` is only the parent SIGKILL deadline). Configure Temporal `shutdownGraceTime` explicitly in worker creation (`worker.ts`) and keep the parent hard-kill deadline strictly greater, so Activities actually drain before escalation. Prefer an IPC `shutdown` message + ack over a bare SIGTERM for intentional rolls.
3. **Bundle-set generation coherence (blocker 3).** Do NOT trigger off `worker.js` alone (risks a mixed `worker.js`/`workflows.js` generation). Deploy writes an **atomic generation manifest LAST**, after all worker artifacts sync, containing hashes for at least `worker.js` and `workflows.js`. Owner watches the **manifest generation id/hash**, not `worker.js` mtime. Two-stable-ticks is a fallback only, not proof of multi-file consistency.
4. **Single-flight roll (blocker 4).** `beatNow()` is fire-and-forget; guard the roll with a single-flight latch so overlapping heartbeat ticks cannot launch concurrent restarts.

### Roll sequence (target)
1. build/sync full bundle set → 2. atomically publish generation manifest last → 3. owner heartbeat notices new generation (manifest hash ≠ recorded) → 4. single-flight intentional `restartChild` requests child shutdown via IPC → 5. Temporal drains for configured `shutdownGraceTime` → 6. parent escalates only after a longer hard deadline → 7. fresh child reaches `ready` → 8. lock `bundle_hash`/generation updated **only after readiness** → 9. crash counter unchanged.

### Files (anticipated)
- `scripts/deploy-local.sh` + `plugin/package.json` (`build:worker`) — emit atomic generation manifest last (hashes of worker.js + workflows.js).
- `worker-lock.ts` — V2 `bundle_hash`/`generation` field.
- `worker-heartbeat.ts` — manifest-generation drift check + single-flight latch seam.
- `worker-multi.ts` / `worker.ts` — first-class `restartChild`; explicit `shutdownGraceTime`; parent deadline > grace.
- `plugin-init.ts` — record spawn-time generation; wire drift→restart callback (OOP only; in-process untouched, AC6).
- Tests (AC7): drift-roll unit test, same-generation no-op, single-flight, crash-counter-unchanged, grace ordering.

### Scope note (surfaced)
Blocker 3 extends the file surface to `scripts/deploy-local.sh` / `build:worker` (manifest emission) — a natural extension of agreed AC2 ("build-emitted stamp"), but broader than "plugin-only." Flagged for planning-gate approval.

### Determinism / boundaries
- No `workflows.ts` worker-bundle import-graph changes; no `defineUpdate`. Hash/manifest/restart logic lives in host-side lifecycle, not workflow-reachable code. No cross-session force-kill; no alive-owner reclaim.
documents.executiveSummary:
## Executive Summary — autoRollStaleWorkerBundle

### Outcome
Redeploying the Advance Temporal worker bundle now automatically rolls running out-of-process workers onto the new code — eliminating the silent stale-worker hazard where every already-running session kept executing old code until manually restarted.

### Why it matters
On Bun hosts (opencode's runtime), each session's worker loads the bundle once at process start; a rebuild/redeploy left running workers stale with no re-election. In a multi-session setup this multiplied — N sessions meant N independently-stale workers running divergent code. This was a correctness/consistency hazard discovered live (3 stale-bundle workers vs a fresh redeploy).

### What was built
- **Atomic generation manifest** emitted last by `build:worker` (SHA-256 over both `worker.js` and `workflows.js`) so rolls trigger on a coherent bundle set, never a half-synced one.
- **Owner-driven self-roll**: the lock-owning session's heartbeat detects generation drift and gracefully respawns its own Node child (first-class `restartChild`, distinct from crash-respawn — crash budget untouched), draining in-flight work within an explicit `shutdownGraceTime` before a longer parent hard-kill deadline.
- **Single-writer `worker.lock`**: the heartbeat is the sole writer; the roll hands the new generation to it — closing a lost-update race caught in acceptance review.

### Verification
53/53 worker suites green; `pnpm run check` green; `build:worker` manifest E2E verified; independent reviewer verdict READY after the single-writer remediation. `workflows.ts` unchanged; no `defineUpdate`; in-process path untouched.

### Risks / follow-ups
- Lock `bundle_generation` lags ≤1 heartbeat (10s) after a roll; only the owner's in-memory monitor reads it (re-roll-immune); an owner crash stops the heartbeat so a stale stamp dies with the lock.
- Follow-up candidate: `scripts/deploy-local.sh` still SIGTERM-bounces deployed workers cross-session — now redundant with owner-driven self-roll.
- Pre-existing, unrelated: `messages.test.ts` "51 signal surface" fails on clean trunk (not touched here).
